flags.why: The term is also established in Southern coastal communities, so Central alone is misleading ([Bà Rịa–Vũng Tàu Museum](https://www.baotangbrvt.org.vn/tuc-tho-ca-ong-cua-ngu-dan-br-vt/)).
The colloquial verb meaning 'to clear off' is the sense learners are most likely to encounter in ordinary conversation.
flags.fix: Put sense 2 first, followed by senses 1, 3 and 4.

flags.why: This old nautical sense denotes the bottom of a boat, not its stern ([Vietnamese dictionary](https://vi.wiktionary.org/wiki/t%E1%BA%BFch)).
The example incorrectly treats tếch as the stern where the boatman stands ([Vietnamese dictionary](https://vi.wiktionary.org/wiki/t%E1%BA%BFch)).
flags.fix: Nặng bồng nhẹ tếch. = Heavy at the top, light at the bottom.

flags.why: The entry omits the familiar disparaging adjective meaning 'uncivilized; savage', used of behavior ([usage example](https://tuoitre.vn/nld/doi-song-tinh-thanh/thu-choi-man-ro-cua-nhung-nguoi-co-tien-20180318173135286.htm)).
A riu is a woven bamboo implement pushed through water to catch shrimp, rather than a trap set and left in place ([Vietnamese dictionary](https://vtudien.com/viet-viet/dictionary/nghia-cua-tu-riu)).
flags.fix: woven bamboo scoop pushed through water to catch small shrimp

flags.why: The example depicts setting a stationary trap instead of pushing the riu through water ([Vietnamese dictionary](https://vtudien.com/viet-viet/dictionary/nghia-cua-tu-riu)).
flags.fix: Ông đẩy cái riu dưới nước để bắt tép. = He pushed the bamboo scoop through the water to catch small shrimp.

flags.why: The parenthetical explanation wrongly identifies the implement used for this action as a trap ([Vietnamese dictionary](https://vtudien.com/viet-viet/dictionary/nghia-cua-tu-riu)).
flags.fix: to catch small shrimp by pushing a woven bamboo scoop through water
